2. The brief facts of the case are as follows:
On 16-05-2023 at about 9.15 p.m., the deceased Pradeep K.S., was riding a Bajaj motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-18-S-5515, observing all the traffic rules and regulations, at Bogadi road, Kalamandira road junction, near Kukkarahalli lake,
Saraswathipuram, Mysuru.

At that time, the driver of car bearing Reg.
No.KA-09-MH-6681, drove the same with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner, endangering to human life and property and dashed against the deceased.

Due to said impact, the deceased has fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries on his head, legs, hands and all over the body.
Immediately after the accident, the deceased was shifted to K.R. Hospital, Mysuru, wherein he succumbed to said injuries.
Earlier to the accident, the deceased was working as Guest Lecturer in Bellur Government ITI College and he was also working as priest and was earning Rs.50,000/- per month.
He was contributing his entire earnings to his family.
Due to untimely death of a sole bread earner, the petitioners are struggling for their livelihood.
The Krishnaraja Traffic Police have registered the case against the driver of the said car for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 304(A) of I.P.C.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.60,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 12% per annum.
3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondents No.1 and 2 have appeared through their counsel.
The respondent No.1 has filed his written statement.
Whereas the respondent No.2 did not choose to file its written statement.
4. The respondent No.1 in his written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.
He has contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.
He has denied the age, income and avocation of the deceased.

He has contended that, on 16-05-2023 the car bearing Reg. No.KA-09-MH-6681 was proceeding from Bogadi towards Mooda, driven by its driver slowly, carefully, on the left side of the road, by observing all the traffic rules and regulations and when the said car was at Kalamandira road junction, near Kukkanahalli lake, the rider of Bajaj motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-18-S-5515, rode the same, without wearing helmet, without driving licence, with high speed, in rash and negligent manner, came from left side cross road and took 'U'
turn to his right side and entered between the said car and ongoing another vehicle and dashed against the car bearing Reg. No.KA-09-MH-6681.
Due to which, he fell down on the road along with his motorcycle and suffered injuries to his head.

Immediately he was shifted to K.R. Hospital,
Mysore.
But, he succumbed to injuries in the said hospital.
The driver of the said car was not at all responsible for the accident.
He was driving the same on the extreme left side of the road.
The entire negligence is on the part of the deceased/rider of the said motorcycle.
But, the petitioners colluding with the jurisdictional police authority and filed a false case against the driver-cum-owner of the said car.
Hence, this respondent is not liable to pay any compensation to the petitioners.
Further it is contended that, the respondent No.1 has insured the said car with the respondent No.2 i.e. SBI General Insurance Company Limited.
If this Court come to the conclusion that, there is negligence on the part of the driver of the said car, the liability is to be fixed on the respondent No.2 insurance company.
For the above denials and contentions, he prayed for dismissal of the petition.

1. Whether the petitioners prove that, deceased Pradeep K.S. S/o Late K.R.
Sathyanarayana Murthy, has succumbed to the injuries sustained in road traffic accident, alleged to have been occurred on 16-05-2023 at about 9.15 p.m., near at Bogadi road, Kalamandira road junction, near Kukkarahalli Lake, Saraswathipuram,
Mysore, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Car bearing Reg.
No. KA-09-MH-6681 ?
2. Whether the petitioners are entitled to compensation?

If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?

Issue No.1: Affirmative Issue No.2: Partly Affirmative Issue No.3: As per the final order, for the following:
REASONS 9. Issue No.1: It is specific case of the petitioners that, on 16-05-2023 at about 9.15 p.m., when the deceased Pradeep K.S., was riding Bajaj motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-18-S- 5515, by observing the traffic rules and regulations, at Bogadi road, Kalamandira road junction, near Kukkarahalli lake,
Saraswathipuram, Mysuru, at that time the driver of offending car bearing Reg.
No.KA-09-MH-6681, drove the same with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the deceased.

Due to said impact, the deceased has fell down and sustained grievous injuries to his head, legs, hands and all over the body and succumbed to said injuries at K.R. Hospital,

Further it is contended that, earlier to the accident, the deceased was working as Guest Lecturer in Bellur Government ITI College and he was also working as priest and was earning a sum of Rs.50,000/- per month.
He was contributing his entire earnings to his family.
Due to untimely death of a sole bread earner, the petitioners are struggling for their livelihood.

10. In order to prove their case, the petitioner No.1 has got examined herself as P.W.1 by filing her examination-in- chief affidavit, wherein she has reiterated the entire averments made in the petition.
Further, in support of their oral evidence, the petitioners have got marked total 19 documents as Ex.P.1 to 19.

Out of the said documents, Ex.P.1 certified copy of F.I.R., Ex.P.2 is certified copy of first information statement, Ex.P.3 is certified copy of spot mahazar, Ex.P.4 is certified copy of sketch, Ex.P.5 is certified copy of seizure mahazar, Ex.P.6 is certified copy of Vidya B R vs Thikshan on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190390866/

11. On meticulously going through the above police documents marked as Ex.P.1 to 13, prima-facie
it reveals that, the alleged accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing No.KA-09-MH-6681 and dashing the same to the motorcycle of the deceased.

Further it reveals that, due to said impact the deceased has fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries to his head, legs, hands and all over the body and succumbed to said injuries on the same day at 11:05 p.m., while undergoing treatment at K.R. Hospital, Mysuru.

The investigation officer in his final report/charge- sheet, which is marked as Ex.P.13, has clearly stated that, the said accident is caused due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing No.KA-09-MH-6681 and dashing the same to the motorcycle of the deceased.

12. At the outset, it is pertinent to note that, in the present case, the date, time and place of accident,
involvement of car bearing No.KA-09-MH-6681 in the said accident, issuance of insurance policy by the respondent No.2 in respect of said vehicle and its validity as on the date of accident, are not in dispute.

But, the respondent No.1 has specifically denied the above averred facts and circumstances of the accident and taken specific defence that, at the relevant point of time of accident the car bearing Reg. No.KA-09-MH-6681 was proceeding from Bogadi towards Mooda, slowly, carefully, on the left side of the road, by observing all the traffic rules and regulations.

When the said car reached Kalamandira road junction, near Kukkanahalli lake, the deceased/rider of Bajaj motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-18-S-5515, rode the same with high speed, in rash and negligent manner, from left side cross road and took 'U' turn to his right side and entered in between the said car and another ongoing vehicle and dashed against the car bearing Reg. No.KA-09- MH-6681 and fell down on the road along with his motorcycle, suffered injuries to his head and succumbed to said injuries while undergoing treatment at K.R. Hospital, Mysore.
The said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the decease and the driver of car bearing Reg. No.KA-09-MH-6681 was not at all responsible for the said accident.
Further, it is contended that, the petitioners colluding with the jurisdictional police have filed a false complaint against the driver-cum-owner of the said car.

But,
the respondent No.1 has failed to establish the above contentions.

Except the self serving statements of R.W.1, who is the none other than the accused/driver-cum-owner of offending car and R.W.2,
who is the authorized person/Manager of the respondent No.2 insurance company, there is no other corroborative oral or documentary evidence placed on record by the respondents to show that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the deceased/rider of motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-18-S-5515 himself and there was no negligence on the part of the driver of offending car.

On the other hand, the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioners clearly establishes that, the said accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg. No.KA-09-MH-6681 and dashing the same to the motorcycle of the deceased.

Though, the learned counsel for respondents have cross- examined P.W.1 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from her mouth which creates doubt on the veracity Vidya B R vs Thikshan on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190390866/
5 of her evidence or which goes to show that, the said accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the deceased himself or there was any contributory negligence on his part in the cause of accident.

13. Further, the Ex.P.3 spot mahazar and Ex.P.4 sketch also clearly speaks that, the said accident has occurred on 39 feet wide Bogadi-Kalamandira road junction, near Kukkarahalli lake,
Saraswathipuram, Mysore, in between offending car bearing Reg. No.KA-09-MH-6681 and the motorcycle bearing No.KA-18-S-5515 of the deceased.
Further, as per the Motor Vehicle Accident Report, which is marked as Ex.P.12, the accident is not caused due to any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident.

When the accident was not caused due to any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident and there was no negligence on the part of the deceased/rider of motorcycle bearing No.KA-18-S-5515, then in the present facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car.

The investigation officer in his Ex.P.13 final report/charge-sheet has clearly stated that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing No.KA-09-MH-6681 and the deceased Pradeep K.S., has succumbed to grievous injuries sustained in the said accident.
Admittedly, the said final report/charge- sheet has not been challenged either by the owner or the driver of offending vehicle.

In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the charge-sheet/final report of the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the date, time and place of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle, rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle and injuries caused to the deceased in the said accident and cause of his death.
14. Further, the Ex.P.8 Post-mortem report, clearly speaks that, the deceased Pradeep K.S., has died due to head injury sustained in the road traffic accident.

There is nothing on record to disbelieve the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioners with respect to injuries sustained by the deceased in the accident in question and cause of his death.

Therefore, in such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can safely be held that, the respondents have failed to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioners, regarding the rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing No.KA-09-MH-6681, injuries sustained by the deceased in the said accident and cause of his death.

15. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
11 SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof as in a criminal case are not required."

Therefore, in the light of observations made in the above cited decisions and for the above stated reasons, this Court is of the considered opinion that, the petitioners have successfully proved through cogent and corroborative evidence that, the deceased Pradeep K.S., has succumbed to grievous injuries sustained in a motor vehicle accident occurred on 16-05-2023 at about 9.15 p.m.,
on Bogadi road - Kalamandira road junction, near Kukkarahalli lake, Saraswathipuram, Mysore, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing No.KA-09-MH-6681.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in Affirmative.
18. Issue No.2:

While answering above issue, for the reasons stated therein, this Court has come to conclusion that, the petitioners have successfully proved that, the accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing No.KA-09-MH-6681 and the deceased Pradeep K.S., has succumbed to grievous injuries sustained in the accident.
Now the petitioners are required to establish that, they are the legal representatives of the deceased Pradeep K.S.
In this regard, they have produced their respective Aadhar cards and Aadhar card of the deceased and ration card of their family, which are marked as Ex.P.14 to 18.
The said documents clearly goes to show that, the petitioner No.1 is wife, petitioners No.2 and 3 are children and petitioner No.4 is mother of the deceased Pradeep K.S.

On the other hand, the relationship of the petitioners with the deceased Pradeep K.S., is not specifically denied by the respondents and even there is no rebuttal evidence placed on record by the respondents with respect to same.

In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the documents produced by the petitioners and hold that, the petitioners are the legal representatives of deceased Pradeep K.S.
19.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of National Insurance Co. V/s Birender, reported in (2020) 11 SCC 356, has clearly held that, "The legal representatives of the deceased could move application for compensation by virtue of clause (c) of Section 166(1).

entities.text: National Insurance Co. V/s Birender, reported in (2020) 11 SCC 356
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The major married son who is also earning and not fully dependant on the deceased, would be still covered by the expression "legal representative" of the deceased.
This Court in Manjuri Bera (supra) had expounded that liability to pay compensation under the Act does not cease because of absence of dependency of the concerned legal representative.
Notably, the expression "legal representative" has not been defined in the Act.
The Tribunal has a duty to make an award, determine the amount of compensation which is just and proper and specify the person or persons to whom such compensation would be paid.
The latter part relates to the entitlement of compensation by a person who claims for the same.
It is thus settled by now that the legal representatives of the deceased have a right to apply for compensation.

Having said that, it must necessarily follow that even the major, married and earning sons of the deceased being legal representatives have a right to apply for compensation and it would be the bounden duty of the Tribunal to consider the application irrespective of the fact whether the concerned legal representative was fully dependent on the deceased and not to limit the claim towards conventional heads only."
20.

According to the ratio laid down in above decision, the legal representatives though not fully dependent on the deceased are entitled to claim compensation under all the heads i.e., under both conventional and non-conventional heads.

In order to determine the compensation, the age,

7 avocation, income, dependency, future prospects of the deceased and other conventional heads are to be ascertained.
21. The compensation towards loss of dependency:

The oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioners clearly establishes that, the petitioners are the legal representatives of the deceased and they were depending on the income of the deceased.
The dependency does not only mean financial dependency.
Even if the dependency is a relevant criterion to claim compensation for loss of dependency, it does not mean financial dependency is the 'ark of the covenant'.
Dependency includes gratuitous service dependency, physical dependency, emotional dependency and psychological dependency.
Hence, this Court is of the opinion that, all the petitioners are entitled for compensation under the head of loss of dependency.

In order to calculate the loss of dependency,
the first step is to determine the age and income of the deceased.
i) Age and income of the deceased : The petitioners have averred that, the age of deceased as on the date of accident was 39 years.

To substantiate the same, the petitioners have produced the Aadhar card and driving licence of the deceased, which are marked as Ex.P.18 and 19, wherein the date of birth of the deceased is mentioned as 02-11-1983.
Admittedly, the accident has taken place on 16- 05-2023.
This clearly geos to show that, on the date of accident the age of the deceased was 39 years.

The petitioners have asserted that, as on the date of accident the deceased was hale and healthy and he was working as Guest Lecturer in Bellur Government ITI College and he was also working as priest and was earning a sum of Rs.50,000/- per month.

But, the petitioners have not produced any document to show that, before accident the deceased Pradeep K.S., was working as Guest Lecturer in Bellur Government ITI College and he was also working as priest and was earning a sum of Rs.50,000/- per month.
In such circumstances, there is no other option before this Court, except to consider the notional income as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.

a) The Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in the cases of, G. T. Basavaraj V/s Niranjan and another, in MFA No.7781/2016, judgment dated 11-08-2022, Ramanna and another V/s Y. B. Mahesh and another in MFA No.140/2017, judgment dated 16-01-2020 and New India Assurance Co. Ltd., V/s Anusaya and others in MFA No.101195/2014, judgment dated 05-01-2023, has clearly held that,
"when the income of the deceased is not proved, then the notional income as per the guidelines issued by Karnataka State Legal Services Authority is to be adopted as the income of the deceased."
b) Admittedly, the accident has taken place in the year 2023.

Further, the annual income of the deceased comes within the exemption limits as per Income Tax Act.
iii) The deduction of personal expenses and calculating the multiplier: The family of the deceased consist of 4 persons i.e., petitioners No.1 to 4.
The total number of dependents of the deceased are four.
Therefore, deduction towards the personal expenses of deceased is taken as 1/4th of the total income, which comes to Rs.67,200/-.
After deducting 1/4th out of total income, towards the personal expenses of the deceased, the annual income of the deceased is held as Rs.2,01,600/-.
iv) As on the date of death, the age of the deceased was 39 years.

As per the guidelines laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and another, reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 S.C., the appropriate multiplier in the present case is taken as 15.

Accordingly, the compensation under the head of loss of dependency is held as Rs.2,01,600/-
x 15 = Rs.30,24,000/-.
v) Compensation under conventional heads:
In the present case, admittedly the petitioner No.1 is wife, petitioners No.2 and 3 are the children and petitioner No.4 is mother of deceased Pradeep K.S.
Hence, the petitioners No.1 to 4 are entitled for compensation under the head of spousal, parental and filial consortium.
As per the guidelines laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd. V/
s Pranay Sethi and others, reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680,

the compensation under the following conventional heads is awarded:
 a) Loss of estate - Rs. 15,000/-
 b) Loss of consortium - Rs. 40,000/- each  c) Funeral expenses - Rs. 15,000/-
The compensation under above heads has to be enhanced 10% for every 3 years.
Seven years have been lapsed from the date of the judgment.

Therefore, the compensation under the above conventional heads is enhanced by 20%, the loss of estate comes to Rs.18,000/-, the loss of spousal,
parental and filial consortium comes to Rs.48,000/- each to petitioners No.1 to 4 and funeral expenses comes to Rs.18,000/-.

Therefore, the petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.32,52,000/-, with interest at the rate of 6% per annum, from the date of petition till its realization.
23. Liability:
Admittedly, as on the date of accident the respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of offending car bearing No.KA-09-MH-6681.
As per Ex.R.2 insurance policy bearing No.TM/PPVBU14273300, issued by the respondent No.2, in respect of offending car bearing No.KA-09-MH-6681 was valid from 03-05-2023 to 02- 05-2024.
As such, the said policy was valid as on the date of accident i.e. 16-05-2023.

Further, as per Ex.P.11 reply to the notice under Section 133 of Motor Vehicles Act, the respondent No.1/driver of the offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-09-MH-6681 was holding valid and effective driving licence to drive light motor vehicle and motorcycle with gear, from 26-04-2021 to 13-08-2031.

As such, as on the date of accident the driver of the offending vehicle was holding valid and effective driving licence and as such there is no breach of any terms and conditions of the insurance policy committed by the insured/respondent No.1.

Further, the evidence placed on record by the petitioners clearly establishes that, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing No.KA-09-MH-6681, the accident has taken place and the deceased Pradeep K.S., has succumbed to grievous injuries sustained in the said accident.
In such circumstances, the respondent No.1 being the owner of offending vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damage caused by the said vehicle.
The respondent No.2 being the insurer of the said vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.1.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
However, the primary liability is on the respondent No.2 to pay the compensation to the petitioners.

Therefore, for the above stated reasons, holding that, the petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.32,52,000/- from the respondent No.2, with interest at the rate of 6% per annum, from the date of petition till its realization.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 in Partly Affirmative.
24. Issue No.3:
In view of the above findings, I proceed to pass the following order:
ORDER The petition is partly allowed with costs.
The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.32,52,000/- (Rupees thirty two lakh fifty two thousand only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till realisation.
The respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the above compensation amount to the petitioners.

However, the primary liability to pay the Vidya B R vs Thikshan on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190390866/

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
When the accident was not caused due to any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident and there was no negligence on the part of the deceased/rider of motorcycle bearing No.KA-18-S-5515, then in the present facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car.
The investigation officer in his Ex.P.13 final report/charge-sheet has clearly stated that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing No.KA-09-MH-6681 and the deceased Pradeep K.S., has succumbed to grievous injuries sustained in the said accident.
In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the charge-sheet/final report of the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the date, time and place of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle, rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle and injuries caused to the deceased in the said accident and cause of his death.
There is nothing on record to disbelieve the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioners with respect to injuries sustained by the deceased in the accident in question and cause of his death.
Therefore, in such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can safely be held that, the respondents have failed to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioners, regarding the rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing No.KA-09-MH-6681, injuries sustained by the deceased in the said accident and cause of his death.
15. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.
Now the petitioners are required to establish that, they are the legal representatives of the deceased Pradeep K.S.
On the other hand, the relationship of the petitioners with the deceased Pradeep K.S., is not specifically denied by the respondents and even there is no rebuttal evidence placed on record by the respondents with respect to same.
In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the documents produced by the petitioners and hold that, the petitioners are the legal representatives of deceased Pradeep K.S.

The Tribunal has a duty to make an award, determine the amount of compensation which is just and proper and specify the person or persons to whom such compensation would be paid.
The oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioners clearly establishes that, the petitioners are the legal representatives of the deceased and they were depending on the income of the deceased.
The dependency does not only mean financial dependency.
Even if the dependency is a relevant criterion to claim compensation for loss of dependency, it does not mean financial dependency is the 'ark of the covenant'.
Dependency includes gratuitous service dependency, physical dependency, emotional dependency and psychological dependency.
Hence, this Court is of the opinion that, all the petitioners are entitled for compensation under the head of loss of dependency.
